ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and on the right side there is a vertical straight line passing through point K and point J, and it is tangent to the circle at point J; from external point K a slanted secant line is drawn, passing in order through points L and M on the circle. What is required is the exterior angle ∠K formed by tangent line KJ and secant line KLM. In the figure, minor arc LJ is labeled 58°, and the farther arc MJ is labeled 164°. Reasoning: According to the tangent-secant exterior angle theorem, the measure of the exterior angle is equal to half the difference of the measures of the two intercepted arcs. Therefore m∠K = (164° - 58°) / 2 = 106° / 2 = 53°. Final answer: 53°.
